scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: I would say 1, YTA (You're The Asshole). As a parent, it's natural to want to visit and check in on your child, especially when they're away at university. However, showing up unannounced can be seen as an overstep of boundaries, especially for a 19-year-old who is trying to establish their independence. Your son had been ignoring your calls, which could be a sign that he needs space, and by showing up unannounced, you may have made him feel like you're not respecting his boundaries. It's also possible that he was busy or stressed with university life, and your visit may have added to his stress. It's great that you're concerned about your son's well-being, but it's essential to respect his autonomy and communicate with him in a way that works for both of you. Perhaps you could have sent him a message or called him to ask if it was a good time to visit, or scheduled a specific time to talk or meet up. This would have given him a sense of control and allowed him to prepare for your visit. Additionally, commenting on the state of his apartment, even if it was meant as a joke, may have come across as judgmental or critical, which could have contributed to his annoyance. It's essential to approach these situations with empathy and understanding, rather than criticism or judgment.
